# Cross-category Chinese remainder and cooperative-lock theorem (v0.19)

Let `A` be the 486-dimensional characteristic-zero native Wilson transport algebra generated by the frozen pair `(g,h)`. Let `H` be the 152-dimensional Q192 Wilson Hecke algebra, and put

`X=A_49`,

`Y=-A_12-A_48-A_59+A_95+A_116+A_125`.

Evaluate the same free word in two letters simultaneously by `g -> g, h -> h` in `A` and by `g -> X, h -> Y` in `H`. Write `B_L` for the image of all words of length at most `L` in `A x H`.

## Theorem 1: filtered direct-product separation

The exact good-prime rank ladder is

| L | words | rank in A | rank in H | rank in A x H | coupling defect |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|0|1|1|1|1|1|
|1|3|3|3|3|3|
|2|7|7|7|7|7|
|3|15|15|15|15|15|
|4|31|31|30|31|30|
|5|63|63|59|63|59|
|6|127|127|113|127|113|
|7|255|255|152|255|152|
|8|511|486|152|511|127|
|9|1023|486|152|638|0|

Because a rank witnessed modulo the certified good prime is a lower bound for the characteristic-zero rank, and 638 is the maximum possible dimension, `B_9=A x H` over characteristic zero. Degree nine is the first complete separation level. At degree eight all 511 formal words remain linearly independent in the paired realization, so there is no common relation through degree eight.

## Theorem 2: a unit-separating relation

The first Hecke relation occurs in degree four and is already one-variable:

`X^4 - 26 X^3 - 131 X^2 + 300 X + 900 = 0`.

The same polynomial evaluated on native `g` is a unit. At `p=1000003` its native unit divisor is nonzero and its arrow rank is `(2,3)`. Therefore no nonzero quotient preserving this primitive generator pairing can be simultaneously a quotient of both algebras: a common quotient would force a unit to map to zero. Equivalently, the two relation ideals are comaximal. The degree-nine rank computation supplies the sharp filtered bound for explicit independent addressing.

## Theorem 3: the degree-eight cooperative lock

At degree eight both coordinate projections are already surjective:

`dim pi_A(B_8)=486`, `dim pi_H(B_8)=152`,

but `dim B_8=511`, not 638. Its pure-native kernel has dimension 359, its pure-Hecke kernel dimension 25, and the residual common coupling quotient has dimension 127. The release freezes explicit 127-row annihilator matrices `sigma_A` and `sigma_H` satisfying

`sigma_A(a)=sigma_H(h)`

for every `(a,h) in B_8` over the good prime.

This is the Wilson analogue of the v30 marginal-insufficiency phenomenon: knowing that both marginals are complete does not imply that the joint state is their direct product.

## Theorem 4: relation transduction

The 25 native relations at degree eight inject into a 25-dimensional pure-Hecke subspace. Pairwise products of those 25 Hecke filters span all 152 dimensions of `H`. Conversely, the 359 Hecke relations inject into a 359-dimensional pure-native subspace. That native family has full arrow rank `(2,3)`, full plus coordinate rank 10, full minus coordinate rank 225, and one left/right multiplication step by `g,h` closes to all 486 native dimensions.

Thus each side's relation space is productive information for the other side rather than dead syntax.

## Theorem 5: optimal minus-channel joint compiler

Restrict degree-eight synchronized words to pure-minus native outputs. With zero, one, two, and three fixed minus channels retained, the Hecke image dimensions are respectively

`25, 100, 152, 152`.

The native image dimensions are

`0, 75, 150, 225`.

Every choice of one channel gives 100 and every choice of two channels gives 152. Hence two fixed minus channels are necessary and sufficient for a **surjective joint word compiler** for every 152-dimensional Hecke filter. However, its native marginal is only 150-dimensional. Any linear section from `H` to this two-channel native marginal therefore has kernel dimension at least two; the release computes the sharper fiber-product count `25-23=2`.

With all three minus channels, the pure-minus native image has dimension 225, the pure-native kernel has dimension 98, and a native-faithful linear section exists. A native-faithful semisimple-only section also exists. These are linear encoding statements, not algebra-embedding claims; Theorem 2 rules out the naive generator-preserving algebra identification.

The distinction is essential: **two minus arrows are optimal for joint execution, three minus arrows are the minimum for a faithful pure-minus native-only encoding.**
